extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in the film The Lion King, film students, and fans
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style, comprehensive encyclopedic entry summarizing production, releases, box-office performance, critical reception, controversies, awards, and legacy of the 1994 animated film The Lion King.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box-office performance / commercial metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of theatrical revenue and commercial success: domestic gross, international gross, worldwide total, opening weekend gross, per-theater average, weekend ranking, re-release grosses, and ticket/admission estimates (including inflation-adjusted figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives concrete examples (e.g., first weekend: $2.7M from 66 locations, $27,664 per theater; initial run worldwide $763.5M; later totals $979M). It cites records (highest-grossing animated film at the time), comparisons (rankings among all films), and ticket estimates (Box Office Mojo's 74M tickets estimate and $812.1M adjusted figure). Re-release performance (3D reissue gross of $94.2M North America, $83.4M overseas) and anniversary re-releases are used to gauge continued commercial strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-theater / limited-release impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics specific to limited openings: per-theater averages, highest opening on under-50 screens, and weekend placing during limited release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: two-theater limited release earned $622,277 in first two days and averaged $793,377 per theater — described as the largest ever achieved during a weekend. Such measures indicate concentrated demand and early positive indicators for wider release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home media release quality and sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of home release formats and features (VHS, LaserDisc, DVD, Blu-ray, 3D Blu-ray, Ultra HD), special/Deluxe/Platinum/Diamond/Signature Editions, bonus features (deleted scenes, director commentary, games, seamless branching), and sales performance (units sold, revenue, first-day sales).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents what features accompanied each edition (e.g., two versions of the film on the Platinum Edition DVD, THX certification, enhanced home theater mix) and sales milestones (VHS best-selling videotape: 4.5M on first day; total VHS releases sold 32M units in North America; Diamond/Blu-ray units and revenue). Use these to judge the strength of ancillary markets and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical presentation & restoration quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of restoration, visual corrections/alterations, and enhanced sound mixes in re-releases and home editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that archived elements and restoration made covering up original deficiencies easier, that an enhanced sound mix was used 'to make the audience feel like they're in the middle of the movie', and that the Platinum Edition featured changes (re-drawn crocodiles). These factors are used to evaluate the technical fidelity and presentation improvements across editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-release strategy and novelty (3D conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the timing, novelty, and market receptiveness to format re-releases (e.g., 3D conversion), and how novelty affects box-office performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ray Subers' analysis cited: the 3D re-release succeeded because the 'notion of a 3D re-release was still fresh and exciting' and timing with the Blu-ray release made it feel timely; subsequent saturation diminished novelty. Use timing, novelty, and marketing to predict re-release success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical consensus / aggregate review metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative aggregates of critical and audience reception such as Rotten Tomatoes approval rating and average score, Metacritic weighted average score, and CinemaScore audience grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page reports Rotten Tomatoes: 92% approval, average 8.5/10; Metacritic: 88/100 ('universal acclaim'); CinemaScore: A+. These aggregated scores summarize critical and audience reception and are commonly used shorthand for acclaim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual and animation artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the film's imagery, animation quality, and visual richness (e.g., 'richly drawn', 'eye-popping thrills', 'some of the richest imagery the studio's animators have produced').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous critics praised the film's visuals and animation (quotes from Variety, Rolling Stone, Entertainment Weekly). Visual artistry is a primary critical criterion for animated features and is often cited in positive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional resonance and storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment of the film's emotional impact, narrative coherence, and storytelling maturity (e.g., 'emotionally stirring', 'resonance', 'coming-of-age tale', comparisons to tragedy/Hamlet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics highlighted emotional impact and storytelling as strengths (Roger Ebert: 'a learning experience as well as an entertainment'; others noted its resonance). Conversely, some reviewers criticized the core story as 'less involving' or 'more noticeably derivative', so narrative originality and depth are central evaluative points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music, songs, and score
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of original songs and score (memorable songs, best original song nominations/wins, soundtrack performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page records awards (Academy Award for Best Original Song 'Can You Feel the Love Tonight', Golden Globe, Grammy nominations/wins) and some critics' views that songs were less memorable compared to other Disney hits. Music quality is measured both by critical commentary and by awards recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice acting and casting performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of voice performances and casting choices (voice actors' contributions to character and critical recognition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites praise for the voice cast and lists awards/nominations related to voice acting (Annie Awards, Young Artist Awards). Voice performance is treated as a distinct criterion in reviews and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production design & technical categories (sound, editing, mixing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of production design, sound editing, sound mixing, and other technical crafts as criteria (nominations/wins in Best Sound, Sound Mixing, Sound Editing, Production Design/Animation supervision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple nominations and wins are listed (e.g., BAFTA Best Sound nomination; Cinema Audio Society nomination/win; Golden Reel Awards for sound editing). These awards indicate industry standards for technical excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and institutional recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition by major industry awards and institutions (Academy Awards, Golden Globes, Grammys, Tony Awards for the stage adaptation, AFI rankings, National Film Registry selection), used as evidence of artistic and cultural merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists wins and nominations across many award bodies and inclusion on lists (TIME, Empire, AFI). Selection for the National Film Registry as 'culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant' is cited as a badge of long-term importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural representation and social impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of social, racial, and class representations and their cultural effects (criticisms that hyenas reflect negative stereotypes; accusations of a 'fascist' narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents critiques about race/class stereotyping and broader ideological readings (e.g., 'fascist narrative' criticism). These considerations are part of evaluating a film's social responsibility and cultural impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / biological portrayal (scientific realism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of animal portrayal accuracy and its effects (e.g., hyena portrayal drawing complaints from hyena biologists, potential impact on conservation perceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyena biologists protested the portrayal (some tongue-in-cheek), claiming possible negative consequences for conservation; the page notes both protests and that the film also sparked interest in hyenas, indicating mixed effects on public understanding of species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality, influence, and plagiarism/ressemblance concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment about the film's originality versus resemblance to prior works (notably Kimba the White Lion), including public/professional protests and debate over whether similarities are inevitable when using animal characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recounts protests in Japan, petitions by cartoonists accusing Disney of plagiarism, responses from creators, and that Tezuka Productions did not pursue litigation. Use historical comparisons and provenance of ideas when evaluating originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchise potential and legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of long-term legacy: sequels, spin-offs, TV series, stage musicals, theme-park attractions, video games, and later remakes indicating cultural endurance and commercial franchising capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article enumerates numerous follow-ups (Timon & Pumbaa series, direct-to-video sequels, The Lion Guard, Broadway musical winning Tonys and becoming a long-running hit, 2019 CGI remake, Black Is King visual album, etc.). The breadth and success of derivative works are used to evaluate enduring influence and franchisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-end and critic list placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement on annual critics' lists and individual rankings (Top 10 lists, honorable mentions) as a signal of critical esteem across publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists many year-end placements (2nd, 5th, 6th, top-10 mentions across newspapers and critics). Aggregated year-end mentions indicate critical standing in a release year.
